Metsä Wood reviewing UK operations amid ‘profitability challenges’
November 25, 2026 | 11:01 am CST
Metsä Wood reviewing UK operations amid ‘profitability challenges’

ESPOO, Finland — Metsä Wood announced the launch of a strategic review of its UK operations due to significant changes in market conditions. The review is expected to be completed in the first half of 2027.

“The UK continues to be one of the key European growth markets for Metsä Wood’s engineered wood products,” said Jussi Noponen, executive vice president of Metsä Wood. “In the strategic review we will explore possibilities to continue on a growth trajectory in engineered wood products, while addressing the profitability challenges of Metsä Wood UK.”

Metsä Wood’s review of UK operations follows the recent completion of statutory negotiations of the company’s personnel in Finland and Estonia that resulted in a reduction of 100 positions in total. In addition, the company said it would implement reorganizations of tasks and operations aimed at improving operational efficiency and strengthening competitiveness. The company said the measures will lead to the termination of employment or a change in duties for 72 people.
Metsä Group’s wood products business, include Kerto® LVL, birch plywood and further processed sawn timber. The company’s U.S. headquarters, Metsä Wood USA, is located in Port Huron, Michigan.

In 2025, the company’s sales totaled EUR 0.5 billion (approximately $565 million). Metsä Group’s parent company Metsäliitto Cooperative is owned by approximately 90,000 Finnish forest owners. The sales of the whole Metsä Group were EUR 5.8 billion (approximately $6.5 billion).

Rich Christianson is the owner of Richson Media LLC, a Chicago-based communications firm focused on the industrial woodworking sector. Rich is the former long-time editorial director and associate publisher of Woodworking Network. During his nearly 35-year career, Rich has toured more than 250 woodworking operations throughout North America, Europe and Asia and has written extensively on woodworking technology, design and supply trends. He has also directed and promoted dozens of woodworking trade shows, conferences and seminars including the Cabinets & Closets Conference & Expo and the Woodworking Machinery & Supply Conference & Expo, Canada’s largest woodworking show.
